terminal_record.title: AFGE and CAP Warn Project 2025 Could Reshape Agencies and Presidential Power
terminal_record.description_short: AFGE describes proposed agency and workforce changes; CAP warns Project 2025 could weaken checks and balances. The sources discuss a blueprint, not completed implementation.
terminal_record.description_medium: AFGE’s July 15, 2024 article describes Project 2025 as a Heritage-organized blueprint backed by more than 100 conservative organizations. It lists proposed agency cuts, privatization, hiring freezes and personnel caps, and cites estimates of up to one million job losses if implemented. CAP frames the plan as a threat to checks and balances. Neither source establishes full implementation.
terminal_record.description_long: The American Federation of Government Employees published an analysis of Project 2025 on July 15, 2024, describing it as a blueprint organized by the Heritage Foundation and backed by more than 100 conservative organizations. AFGE lists proposed agency and program cuts, privatization, hiring freezes, and caps on personnel. It says some estimates put potential federal job losses as high as one million if the proposals were implemented; that is a conditional estimate, not a count of jobs already lost. The Center for American Progress presents a related warning in its article “Project 2025 Would Destroy the U.S. System of Checks and Balances and Create an Imperial Presidency.” Its accessible opening describes a plan to give presidents nearly unlimited power, but does not document completed implementation. These sources support an entry about critics’ warnings and the blueprint’s proposed direction. They do not establish that every major component became law, that the United States completed a transition to autocracy, or what current legal and practical effects resulted. The title and descriptions are narrowed to the proposal and attributed assessments.
